title: Topoi and derived categories as organizing concepts
notes: I.~M.~Gelfand identifies \ru{Топос} and \ru{Производная категория} as two primary concepts of category theory.
statement: This is a pedagogical judgement, not a theorem that category theory has precisely two basic notions. A Grothendieck topos is a category equivalent to sheaves of sets on a site; for an abelian category \(\mathcal A\), its derived category inverts quasi-isomorphisms of complexes.
reconstruction: The definitions clarify the two names; the evaluative word primary remains the speaker's judgement.
fate: The frameworks predate this lecture: \citet[Expos\'e~IV]{sga41972topos} and \citet[Chapter~I]{hartshorne1966residues}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Both frameworks remain established; the notebook supplies no testable exclusivity claim.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Describe algebraic vector bundles on projective space
notes: \ru{Задача: описать все алгебраические расслоения над} \(\mathbb P^n\), for example over \(\mathbb C\). The subsequent theorem specifies the intended description by exterior-algebra modules.
statement: For each integer \(n\geq0\), describe the isomorphism classes of finite-rank algebraic vector bundles on \(\mathbb P^n_{\mathbb C}\). In the sense actually developed in the notes, the answer sought is a bijection with stable isomorphism classes of proper finite-dimensional graded \(\Lambda(\mathbb C^{n+1})\)-modules.
reconstruction: The meaning of describe is fixed by the theorem that follows, rather than by an unrecorded demand for a finite list of invariants.
fate: Answered in this representation-theoretic sense by \citet[Theorem~1]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978bundles}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The correspondence is established. It is not a numerical enumeration of all moduli spaces, and does not imply a solution of every later vector-bundle classification question.

title: Projective space is the scalar quotient of a punctured vector space
notes: \(\Xi\) is called affine space and \(\xi\sim\alpha\xi\), \(\alpha\in\mathbb C^*\), \(\xi\ne0\); the quotient is \(\mathbb P^n\).
statement: Let \(\Xi\) be a complex vector space of dimension \(n+1\). Then \(\mathbb P(\Xi)=(\Xi\setminus\{0\})/\mathbb C^*\) parametrizes its one-dimensional vector subspaces. The chosen origin and linear structure are essential; a bare affine space does not carry the displayed scalar action canonically.
reconstruction: Replace the informal affine-space wording by a vector space and retain the explicit exclusion of zero.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Standard, with the puncture and dimension made explicit.

title: The negatively graded exterior algebra
notes: \(\Lambda=\{\xi_0,\ldots,\xi_n\mid\xi_i\xi_j+\xi_j\xi_i=0\}\), \(\dim\Lambda=2^{n+1}\), and \(\Lambda=\bigoplus_{k=0}^{n+1}\Lambda_{-k}\).
statement: Over \(\mathbb C\), put \(\Lambda=\bigwedge\Xi\) with \(\deg\xi=-1\) for \(\xi\in\Xi\). Then \(\Lambda_{-k}=\bigwedge^k\Xi\), \(\dim\Lambda_{-k}=\binom{n+1}{k}\), and the total dimension is \(2^{n+1}\). In characteristic two one must impose \(\xi_i^2=0\) explicitly; the notes use characteristic zero.
reconstruction: The binomial dimensions and characteristic qualification spell out the displayed presentation.
fate: The algebra is classical; these conventions are also fixed in \citet[\S2]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978bundles}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: An established definition. The sign of the grading must be retained in subsequent shifts.

title: Finite graded representations of the exterior algebra
notes: Objects are \(V=\bigoplus_jV_j\), \(\dim V<\infty\), with \(\Lambda_{-k}V_j\subset V_{j-k}\).
statement: A finite-dimensional graded left \(\Lambda\)-module has a finite-support \(\mathbb Z\)-grading and degree-zero module morphisms. For a generator \(\xi\), multiplication gives \(V_j\to V_{j-1}\). Both the module and every free summand used later are graded.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The grading is essential; ungraded stable equivalence would be a different assertion.

title: A complex for every nonzero exterior generator
notes: \(L_\xi(V)=\{\cdots\to V_1\xrightarrow{\xi}V_0\xrightarrow{\xi}V_{-1}\to\cdots\}\), because \(\xi^2=0\).
statement: For \(\xi\in\Xi\setminus\{0\}\), let \(d_j(v)=\xi v\) on \(V_j\). Then \(d_{j-1}d_j=0\), and \(H_j(L_\xi(V))=\ker(d_j)/\operatorname{im}(d_{j+1})\). This is a bounded chain complex of finite-dimensional vector spaces.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: A standard component of the BGG construction; the displayed differential is literally correct.

title: Proper modules: fibre homology concentrated in degree zero
notes: \(V\) is \ru{правильный} if \(H_i(L_\xi(V))=0\) for every \(\xi\ne0\) and every \(i\ne0\).
statement: A finite-dimensional graded \(\Lambda\)-module is proper when each nonzero \(\xi\in\Xi\) gives homology only in degree zero. No requirement that \(H_0\) be nonzero is imposed: free modules are included.
reconstruction: The terminology must not be confused with a faithful representation in ordinary ring theory.
fate: This is the condition called faithful in the English translation of \citet[\S2]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978bundles}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established. Here faithful is a translation of the special definition, not injectivity of the action homomorphism.

title: The Euler characteristic fixes the fibre rank
notes: For proper \(V\), \(\dim H_0(L_\xi(V))\) is constant and equals \(\sum_i(-1)^i\dim V_i\).
statement: For a bounded finite-dimensional complex, \[\sum_i(-1)^i\dim H_i=\sum_i(-1)^i\dim V_i.\] Thus properness implies \(\dim H_0(L_\xi(V))=\sum_i(-1)^i\dim V_i\), independently of nonzero \(\xi\).
reconstruction: For an independent check, write each dimension as boundary rank plus homology dimension plus the preceding boundary rank; the alternating boundary terms cancel.
fate: An elementary Euler-characteristic identity, used in the construction of \citet[\S2]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978bundles}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Correct. Constant fibre dimension is one part of the vector-bundle argument, not a substitute for its algebraicity.

title: The homology spaces form an algebraic vector bundle
notes: The assignment \(\xi\mapsto H_0(L_\xi(V))\) is the same for \(\xi\) and \(\alpha\xi\); later \(\Phi(V)=H^0(\mathcal L(V))\) is defined.
statement: For a proper module over \(\Lambda(\Xi)\), the complex \(\mathcal L^j(V)=V_{-j}\otimes\mathcal O(j)\) on \(\mathbb P(\Xi)\), with differential \(\sum x_i\otimes\xi_i\), has zero cohomology sheaves outside degree zero, and \(\Phi(V)=\mathcal H^0(\mathcal L(V))\) is locally free. Its fibre at \([\xi]\) identifies with \(H_0(L_\xi(V))\).
reconstruction: Algebraic dependence and local splitting are supplied by the displayed bundle complex: fibre exactness permits elimination of invertible minors at both ends until only a locally free degree-zero term remains.
fate: The precise assertion precedes Theorem~1 of \citet{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978bundles}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established with sheaf cohomology understood as cohomology of this complex, not global cohomology of its terms.

title: Free exterior-algebra modules give the zero bundle
notes: For \(V=\Lambda\), all \(H_i(L_\xi(V))\) vanish. Direct sums and grading shifts give \ru{трив. расслоение}, after the more precise phrase \ru{нулевое расслоение}.
statement: Every finite graded free \(\Lambda\)-module \(P\) satisfies \(H_i(L_\xi(P))=0\) for all \(i\) and \(\xi\ne0\), hence \(\Phi(P)=0\), the rank-zero bundle. It does not yield every positive-rank trivial bundle.
reconstruction: Choose \(a\in\Xi^*\) with \(a(\xi)=1\). Interior multiplication \(\iota_a\) satisfies \(\iota_a(\xi\wedge-)+\xi\wedge\iota_a=1\), proving acyclicity in all dimensions. Direct sums and shifts preserve it.
fate: This is the acyclic exterior Koszul complex; see also \citet[\S2]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978bundles}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Correct after disambiguating trivial as zero. The contraction identity is checked in the critical-verification appendix.

title: Every algebraic vector bundle has a proper-module model
notes: Theorem~1, repeated as Theorem~\(1^{\prime}\)(1), says every bundle is \(\Phi(V)\) for a proper \(V\).
statement: For every finite-rank algebraic vector bundle \(\mathcal E\) on \(\mathbb P^n_{\mathbb C}\), there is a finite-dimensional graded proper module \(V\) over \(\bigwedge\mathbb C^{n+1}\) with \(\Phi(V)\cong\mathcal E\).
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established; the public-talk evidence in this package is February 1978, not February 1977.

title: Uniqueness is stable graded isomorphism
notes: Theorem~\(1^{\prime}\)(2) states \(\Phi(V)\cong\Phi(V^{\prime})\) iff \(V\oplus P\cong V^{\prime}\oplus P^{\prime}\) for free \(P,P^{\prime}\).
statement: For two finite-dimensional graded proper \(\Lambda\)-modules, their associated bundles are isomorphic exactly when there exist finite graded free modules \(P,P^{\prime}\) with a degree-zero \(\Lambda\)-module isomorphism \(V\oplus P\simeq V^{\prime}\oplus P^{\prime}\). The two added free modules need not coincide.
reconstruction: The grading and the properness of both modules are carried over from the preceding definition.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established. The stronger categorical form quotients morphisms factoring through graded free modules.

title: An independently obtained related theorem of Beilinson
notes: The theorem is attributed to Bernstein, S.~Gelfand and I.~Gelfand, followed by \ru{независимо близкий рез. Бейлинсон}.
statement: The supported historical assertion is a related independent construction, not identity of all formulations. Beilinson describes the derived category of coherent sheaves on \(\mathbb P^n\) through finite complexes formed from \(\mathcal O(-i)\) or \(\Omega^i(i)\), \(0\leq i\leq n\).
reconstruction: The derived-category formulation is taken from the checked publication; the notebook only reports a similar result. The student-year description is not independently verified.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Both correspondences are established; their relationship has constructive formulations in \citet[Theorem~6.1]{eisenbudfloystadschreyer2003exterior}.

title: Twisting line bundles and homogeneous regular functions
notes: \(O(k)\) has sections described as homogeneous rational functions of degree \(k\); \(O(1)\) is called the bundle with a section, and then the Hopf bundle, with \(O(-1)\) offered as an alternative.
statement: For \(n\geq1\), let \(\mathcal O(-1)\) be the tautological line bundle and \(\mathcal O(1)\) its dual. A section of \(\mathcal O(k)\) over a Zariski open \(U\subset\mathbb P(\Xi)\) is a homogeneous regular function of degree \(k\) on its preimage in \(\Xi\setminus\{0\}\). On \(x_i\ne0\), division by \(x_i^k\) gives a regular scalar function and proves local rank one. In particular \(H^0(\mathcal O(1))=\Xi^*\). The case \(n=0\) is a point, on which all twists are isomorphic.
reconstruction: Rational sections must be regular on the specified open set. The separately dated P000758 provides corroborating anti-Hopf wording and asks the elementary rank-one question; it is not a second occurrence assigned to record 437.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The convention is settled by the homogeneous-degree definition. Having a nonzero section does not uniquely characterize O(1).

title: The global linear complex on projective space
notes: \(\mathcal L_j=V_{-j}\otimes O(j)\); on sections \((df)(\xi)=\xi f(\xi)\), giving \(\mathcal L(V)\).
statement: For any finite graded \(\Lambda\)-module \(V\), define \(\mathcal L^j(V)=V_{-j}\otimes\mathcal O(j)\) and \(d=\sum_{i=0}^n x_i\otimes\xi_i\). The tensor \(\sum x_i\otimes\xi_i\) is independent of dual bases. Since the \(x_i\) commute and the \(\xi_i\) anticommute and square to zero, \(d^2=0\). The sheaf morphisms have the indicated twists, and the complex is bounded.
reconstruction: Superscripts distinguish cohomological degree from the negative internal grading; the differential formula itself is the notebook formula.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established. An arbitrary module gives a complex; properness is needed for a single vector bundle.

title: Twisting by O(1) is a shifted cosyzygy
notes: What does \(\mathcal E\mapsto\mathcal E\otimes O(1)\) mean for modules? For \(0\to V\to P\to V^{\prime}\to0\), \(P\) free, set \(W_j=V^{\prime}_{j+1}\); then \(\Phi(W)=\Phi(V)\otimes O(1)\).
statement: Let \(V\) be proper and \(0\to V\to P\to V^{\prime}\to0\) exact in finite graded \(\Lambda\)-modules, with \(P\) graded free. Then the grading shift \(W_j=V^{\prime}_{j+1}\) is proper and \(\Phi(W)\cong\Phi(V)(1)\). Such a free embedding exists because the finite-dimensional exterior algebra is Frobenius and its graded projectives are injective.
reconstruction: The long exact fibre-homology sequence gives \(H_i(V^{\prime})\cong H_{i-1}(V)\). Hence \(W\) is proper. Globally \(\mathcal L^j(W)=\mathcal L^{j-1}(V^{\prime})(1)\); the exact sequence gives the asserted degree-zero cohomology. This also checks the sign of the shift.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established. Both the cosyzygy and internal grading shift are needed.

title: Large positive twists are globally generated
notes: For sufficiently large \(N\), Serre’s theorem gives enough sections of \(\mathcal E\otimes O(N)\) through every vector in every fibre, called \ru{обильное расслоение}.
statement: If \(\mathcal E\) is coherent on \(\mathbb P^n_{\mathbb C}\), there is \(N_0\) such that for every \(N\geq N_0\) the evaluation map \(H^0(\mathcal E(N))\otimes\mathcal O\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal E(N)\) is surjective. The section space is finite-dimensional. The property used here is global generation, not the definition of an ample vector bundle.
reconstruction: The evaluation formulation specifies the phrase many sections. Ampleness and generation are different properties.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established; in an inverse BGG algorithm the twist must also be sufficiently regular for exactness.

title: The graded section module and coordinate multiplications
notes: \(C_N=\Gamma(\mathbb P^n,\mathcal E(N))\), \(\dim\Gamma(O(1))=n+1\), and \(X_i:C_N\to C_{N+1}\) multiplies by the dual coordinate \(x_i\).
statement: Put \(S=\operatorname{Sym}(\Xi^*)\) and \(C_{\geq N}=\bigoplus_{m\geq N}H^0(\mathcal E(m))\), for a vector bundle \(\mathcal E\) on \(\mathbb P(\Xi)\). Multiplication by \(x_i\in\Xi^*\) defines commuting maps between successive components; for a sufficiently large truncation this is a finite graded \(S\)-module.
reconstruction: Finite generation refers to the graded module of all sufficiently large twists, not to a single vector space with a polynomial action.
fate: The classical construction is in \citet[Chapter~III]{serre1955coherent}. Finite generation is stated precisely in \citet[Lemma~30.14.1(5)]{stacks2026projective}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Standard. The commutation relations imply the square-zero identity in the ensuing Koszul-dual complex.

title: Recovering a module from two consecutive section spaces
notes: The notes put \(V=C_N\otimes\Lambda\), \(V^{\prime}=C_{N+1}\otimes\Lambda\), \(\partial(c\otimes\lambda)=\sum_iX_i(c)\otimes\xi_i\lambda\), and \(W=\ker\partial\), followed by \(N\) inverse shifts using free covers.
statement: Let \(\mathcal E\) be an algebraic vector bundle on \(\mathbb P(\Xi)\), \(S=\operatorname{Sym}(\Xi^*)\), and \(M=\bigoplus_{m\geq0}H^0(\mathcal E(m))\). Choose an integer \(N>\max\{0,\operatorname{reg}M\}\). In cohomological degree \(m\), put \(R(M)^m=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(\Lambda,M_m)\), with internal component \[R(M)^m_t=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(\Lambda_{m-t},M_m).\] The differential is \((d_Rf)(\lambda)=\sum_i x_i f(\xi_i\lambda)\); it preserves internal degree. The tail with \(m\geq N\) is exact in degrees strictly greater than \(N\). Adjoin a minimal graded free resolution of its initial kernel, retaining these cohomological indices, to obtain the everywhere exact Tate complex \(T(\mathcal E)\). Then \[V=\ker\bigl(T(\mathcal E)^0\longrightarrow T(\mathcal E)^1\bigr)\] is a finite-dimensional graded proper module and \(\Phi(V)\cong\mathcal E\).
reconstruction: Both gradings, the regularity bound and the degree-zero kernel are supplied here; the notebook gives an abbreviated two-section-space construction. In the modern dual-module convention, \((a\cdot f)(\lambda)=f(\lambda a)\), so \(d_R\) is a degree-zero \(\Lambda\)-module map. By contrast the notebook's raw tensor formula has internal degree \(-1\) and anticommutes with the generators, although its kernel is still a graded submodule. For \(n=0\), \(\mathcal E=\mathcal O\), its raw kernel is \(\mathbb C\xi_0\) in degree \(-1\), hence is not proper. The dual free module \(\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(\Lambda,\mathbb C)\) has degrees \(0,\ldots,n+1\), and is noncanonically \(\Lambda(-(n+1))\) under \(Q(a)_j=Q_{a+j}\); omitting that shift changes the answer.
fate: The notebook sketch belongs to the inverse BGG construction; compare \citet[\S~4]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978bundles}. The explicit conventions above are \citet[\S~2, Corollary~2.4, Theorem~3.7 and the construction in \S~4]{eisenbudfloystadschreyer2003exterior}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The construction is established, but the notebook omits the grading of the two free modules; its unqualified kernel cannot be certified as already proper.

title: Vector bundles must be enlarged to coherent sheaves
notes: I.~M.~Gelfand says classification of bundles is not quite the right problem because they do not form an abelian category; one must allow fibre dimensions to vary and introduce sheaves.
statement: For \(n\geq1\), finite-rank locally free sheaves on \(\mathbb P^n\) are not an abelian category with the inherited sheaf morphisms: multiplication by a nonzero linear form gives \(\mathcal O(-1)\to\mathcal O\) whose sheaf cokernel is the structure sheaf of a hyperplane and is not locally free. Coherent sheaves form an abelian category. For \(n=0\), vector bundles are finite-dimensional vector spaces and already form an abelian category.
reconstruction: More intrinsically, that multiplication map is monic and epic within the category of locally free sheaves, since a map from its torsion cokernel to a locally free sheaf is zero, but is not an isomorphism on the hyperplane. An abelian category is balanced, so it cannot have such a map. The point case is exceptional.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Correct with the positive-dimensional qualification; variable fibre rank alone is not a definition of a coherent sheaf.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Serre correspondence is a quotient by finite-dimensional graded modules
notes: The notes equate sheaves on \(\mathbb CP^n\) with finitely generated graded \(\mathbb C[x_0,\ldots,x_n]\)-modules up to finitely many homogeneous components.
statement: For \(S=\mathbb C[x_0,\ldots,x_n]\) with standard grading, sheafification induces an equivalence \(\operatorname{grmod}(S)/\operatorname{fdim}(S)\simeq\operatorname{Coh}(\mathbb P^n_{\mathbb C})\). Here the numerator has finitely generated graded modules and degree-zero maps, and the denominator is its Serre subcategory of finite-dimensional modules. A quasi-inverse is the nonnegative graded section module followed by passage to the quotient.
reconstruction: A quotient category replaces the informal phrase ignoring finitely many components; coherence is an essential omitted hypothesis.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established. It concerns algebraic coherent sheaves; arbitrary sheaves are not covered.

title: Sheafification through degree-zero localization
notes: On \(E_i=\{x_i\ne0\}\), \(\Gamma(E_i,L)=\{m/x_i^s:\deg m=s,\ m\in M\}\).
statement: For a graded \(S\)-module \(M\), set \(\widetilde M(D_+(x_i))=(M_{x_i})_0\). Homogeneous fractions have \(\deg m=s\); equality is equality in the localization, so elements killed by powers of \(x_i\) vanish. The localization maps on overlaps glue these affine modules into a quasi-coherent sheaf, coherent if \(M\) is finitely generated.
reconstruction: The equivalence relation on fractions and the gluing maps are implicit in the notebook.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established and literally correct when the braces mean localized fractions.

title: Shifting the polynomial module yields O(N)
notes: \(O(N)\) arises from \(M=\mathbb C[x_0,\ldots,x_n]\) with \(M_i=S_{i+N}\).
statement: Define \(S(N)_i=S_{i+N}\). Then \(\widetilde{S(N)}\cong\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^n}(N)\). Locally a homogeneous numerator of degree \(s+N\), divided by \(x_i^s\), has homogeneous degree \(N\), exactly the earlier section convention.
reconstruction: The local fraction check compares the final formula with the earlier homogeneous-function definition.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Correct; this independently fixes the sign of the polynomial-module shift.
